title: BTC Cycles & Sector Rotation: 2013–2026 and the 2026–27 Setup
bottom_line: BTC is 12 months past its $126,080 peak (6 Oct 2025), bottomed near $59,300 in June 2026 (-53%), and trades around $81,000–85,000 in late October 2026 — a milder bear than the -77% to -87% of prior cycles. Four cycles of data say the same thing each time: BTC leads the recovery for 12–18 months, and the alt sector that wins is the one with a new product category + real on-chain usage + a launch-platform that lets retail mint thousands of tokens (ICOs 2017, DeFi/NFT/alt-L1s 2021, memecoins/AI agents 2024). The sectors that won on fundamentals rather than pure speculation (DeFi 2020, perp DEXs 2025, RWA 2024–26) are the ones still standing a cycle later.

For 2026–27 the strongest candidates, ranked by metric evidence rather than hype, are: (1) on-chain finance with real revenue — perp DEXs and fee-sharing tokens (Hyperliquid alone passed $1.4bn cumulative revenue in Oct 2026); (2) stablecoin / payments infrastructure (~$300bn supply, now a regulated rail); (3) RWA and tokenized stocks ($38.6bn on-chain ex-stablecoins, up ~4x in 18 months); (4) prediction markets ($50bn+ monthly volume in July 2026, but no liquid token yet); (5) a second AI x crypto wave (agent payments, x402, Bittensor); with privacy/ZK and consumer/TON as the speculative sleeve. Historically, year two after a peak (2015, 2019, 2023) is a BTC-dominant, narrow-breadth recovery — alts broadly lagged until the halving year. Treat 2026–27 as the accumulation window for the sectors above, not as the parabolic phase.

anatomy.intro: Each cycle has followed the same shape — bottom roughly 12–18 months before the halving, peak 12–18 months after it, then a 1-year bear — but the multiples shrink and the drawdowns soften every time. Pre-2024 figures are approximate (exchange prices varied); 2025–26 figures are from the sources below.
rows: June 2026 low, or a retest in Q4 2026
anatomy.after: What changed in cycle 4: spot ETFs (about $26bn of net inflows in 2025), corporate treasuries and a $4tn total market cap at the Q3 2025 peak meant the top was a [grind rather than a blow-off](https://www.tradingview.com/news/99Bitcoins:37c5f55d3094b:0-crypto-market-2025-year-end-review-expert-insights/), and the bear was shallow. As of [19 October 2026](https://www.openpr.com/news/4667045/bitcoin-price-prediction-october-2026-btc-holds-near-81k-as) BTC sits at about $81,000–82,000, roughly 35% below the high and 40% above the June low, back above its 200-day average (about $70,000–72,000). The open question analysts are split on is whether June 2026 was the low or whether Q4 2026 (the 900-days-post-halving window that marked the 2018 and 2022 lows) delivers one more retest — [NYDIG's](https://www.coingecko.com/learn/bitcoin-price-predictions-expert-forecasts) scenario puts a 2022-style depth at $38,000–39,000, while most desks' bear cases sit at $53,000–60,000.

cycles.heading: Cycle 1 (2012–14): forks, payment coins and the first "altcoin season"
cycles.intro: There were only a few hundred coins and no sector taxonomy; the winners were Bitcoin forks with one tweak (faster blocks, a new hash algorithm, proof-of-stake) plus the first non-fork ledgers. Figures are approximate, taken from the exchanges of the time.

rows.What drove it: Scrypt mining (GPU-friendly), first listings on Mt. Gox/BTC-e
First proof-of-stake and asset-issuance chains; Mastercoin ran the first ICO (Jul 2013)
Reddit tipping culture — the template every later meme cycle reused
Post-Silk Road demand for private payments; the privacy sector peaked after BTC

cycles.after: Burst duration: the altcoin phase ran about 3 months (Nov 2013–Feb 2014) — far shorter than later cycles — and nearly every coin lost 90%+ by 2015. Only LTC, XRP, DOGE and the privacy coins survived into the next cycle. Common metrics barely existed: no TVL or fees to measure, so the signals were exchange listings, hash-rate and Bitcointalk thread activity.

cycles.heading: Cycle 2 (2015–18): the ICO / smart-contract cycle
cycles.intro: Ethereum turned token issuance into a product. The 2017 run was the first time the alt market cap exceeded Bitcoin's — BTC dominance fell from 87% to 33% (Jan 2018) — and most sector tops came 3–5 weeks after BTC's December 2017 high. Figures are approximate.

rows.Top 5 coins: ETH, NEO (Antshares), EOS, ADA, QTUM (also LSK, ETC, XLM)
rows.What drove it: ICO demand — ~$6bn raised in 2017; each new platform promised cheaper/faster ICOs

rows.Top 5 coins: XRP, XLM, NANO (RaiBlocks), XVG (Verge), TRX
rows.What drove it: "Banks will use it" narrative; Korean/Japanese retail exchanges (Bithumb, Coincheck)

rows.Top 5 coins: XMR, DASH, ZEC, XVG, PIVX
rows.What drove it: Exchange delistings had not started; darknet + "digital cash" narrative

rows.What drove it: Fee discounts + burn — the first real token cash-flow mechanism

cycles.after: Burst duration: the alt phase ran about 12 months (Mar 2017–Jan 2018) with two spikes — May–Jun 2017 (ICO platforms) and Dec 2017–Jan 2018 (payment coins and small-caps, when BTC was already topping). The top-10 gainers of 2017 by % (approximate, from period market data) were Verge, XRP, NEM, Ardor, Stellar, Dash, Ethereum, Golem, BNB and Litecoin — 7 of the 10 were payment or platform coins, and 8 of the 10 made new lows in 2018 (-90% to -99%). Metrics that worked: ICO raise size, exchange listings (Binance/Bithumb), Google search volume (the "bitcoin" search peak coincided with the December 2017 top to the week), GitHub commits. Backers: ICO treasuries and early VC (Polychain, Pantera, DCG); chain: almost everything was an ERC-20 or its own L1.

cycles.heading: Cycle 3 (2019–22): DeFi, alt-L1s, NFTs/GameFi and memecoins
cycles.intro: This was the first cycle with measurable on-chain fundamentals (TVL, fees, users), and the first with a double top (Apr and Nov 2021). Sector leadership rotated four times in 18 months. Figures are approximate (CoinGecko/DefiLlama period data).

cycles.after: Burst durations were 3–5 months per sector, and the whole alt window lasted about 16 months (Aug 2020–Nov 2021). The sectors with real cash flow (DeFi blue chips, exchange tokens) fell 80–90% in 2022 but survived and recovered; those with none (GameFi, metaverse land, LUNA, FTT) lost 95–100%. Top-10 coins by market cap at the Nov 2021 peak: BTC, ETH, BNB, USDT, SOL, ADA, XRP, DOT, DOGE, AVAX — five of them did not exist or were sub-$1bn two years earlier. Backers: a16z, Paradigm, Multicoin, Jump, FTX/Alameda (SOL ecosystem), Binance Labs; chain: Ethereum for DeFi/NFTs, then BSC, Solana, Avalanche and Polygon for the "cheap alternative" trade.

cycles.heading: Cycle 4 (2023–25): memecoins, AI agents, RWA, perp DEXs and treasuries
cycles.intro: The first ETF-era cycle. Retail rotated through launchpads (pump.fun, Virtuals) while institutions bought BTC/ETH and tokenized Treasuries, so the sector leaderboard split: speculative narratives won 2024, fundamentals-led narratives won 2025. CoinGecko's average return across each narrative's 10 largest tokens: [2024](https://forklog.com/en/ai-leads-crypto-market-gains-in-2024-reports-coingecko/) — AI +2,940%, memecoins +2,185%, RWA +820%, L1 +142%, DePIN +135%, DeFi +101%, GameFi +14%, L2 -21% (BTC +125%); [2025](https://www.coingecko.com/research/publications/most-profitable-crypto-narratives) — RWA +186%, L1 +80%, "Made in USA" +31%, memecoins -32%, AI -50%, with only RWA and L1 positive in both years. Coin prices below are approximate (CoinGecko).

cycles.after: Burst durations compressed to 6–12 weeks per narrative, and leadership rotated faster than in 2021 — the market was liquid enough to run a memecoin, an AI-agent and an RWA cycle inside four months (Nov 2024–Feb 2025). Most 2024 winners (memes, AI agents) peaked in January 2025, nine months before BTC's top in October 2025, and are down 60–90% from peak; the 2025 winners (HYPE, RWA, L1s, DATs) peaked with or after BTC. Backers: the fair-launch/no-VC model (HYPE, pump.fun) beat VC-backed launches on performance; a16z, Paradigm, Pantera, Binance Labs/YZi, and TradFi (BlackRock, Franklin Templeton, Apollo) backed the RWA side. Chains: Solana and Base for retail speculation; Ethereum for RWA (47% of value); own-chain for perps (Hyperliquid L1).

cross_cycle.intro: Every cycle's biggest winner was a new way to issue or trade tokens (fork → ICO → yield farm/NFT mint → launchpad), and every cycle also had one "serious" sector that survived into the next. The alt window has shortened from 12–16 months to a series of 6–12-week bursts, and peak multiples have fallen roughly 10x per cycle as the market cap grew.

metrics.intro: Across the four cycles the winning sectors shared the same signature: a step-change in a usage metric before price, a launch primitive that let retail participate, concentrated liquidity on one chain, and a search-volume peak that marked the top rather than the start. The table shows which metric mattered, what the winners looked like on it, and the threshold that has historically marked the blow-off.

metrics.after: The metrics divide cleanly into two groups: fundamentals (TVL, fees, usage, utility) decide which sector survives, while attention metrics (search volume, launch counts, new wallets) decide when it tops. The 2024–25 cycle added a new one — protocol revenue returned to holders — which did not exist at scale in any prior cycle and is the main reason HYPE held up while every agent token did not.

The history says the speculative winner of the next parabolic phase (2028–29 on the halving clock) is usually not visible yet; what is visible in 2026 is which sectors are compounding through the bear, which is where the mid-cycle (2019-, 2023-style) returns came from.

candidates.after: What is deliberately not on the list: digital-asset-treasury equities (the 2025 trade is over — the mNAV premium that made it work has compressed), first-wave AI-agent tokens, and 2024-vintage memecoins. The memecoin primitive itself will return — it has in every cycle — but historically on a new launchpad or chain, not the last cycle's survivors; watch TON mini-apps and whichever chain next hosts pump.fun-style issuance. Probability-weighted, the 2026–27 leaderboard most likely looks like 2019–20's: BTC and the L1 beta first, then the fundamentals sectors (1–3) compounding quietly, with one speculative burst (4, 5 or 7) of 2–3 months somewhere in 2027.

signals.timing: On the halving clock, 2027 is the "2019/2023" year: BTC rose 95% (2019) and 155% (2023) off its lows but alts broadly lagged, and the true alt season came in the halving year and after. If June 2026 was the low, a 2027 exit window sits mid-cycle on that clock — so a target like a BTC reclaim of its old high in 2027 is consistent with 2019 (which reached +300% from the low) and 2023 (+200%), but a broad, 2021-style alt blow-off by mid-2027 would be ahead of every prior cycle. The sectors above are the ones that produced mid-cycle returns anyway (IEOs/BNB in 2019; AI, L2 airdrops and SOL in 2023).
signals.intro: Watch these, in order of how early they fire:
items: A new issuance primitive gaining >1,000 launches/day on any chain (pump.fun in 2024 was visible 6 months before the meme top).
Per-chain stablecoin supply and DEX volume turning up for 8+ weeks — that identified Solana in late 2023.
Perp-DEX revenue and RWA AUM continuing to rise while prices fall (currently true for both) — the DeFi-2020 setup.
Spot + ETF volume sustainably above about $10bn/day (recently about $6.8bn); ETF net inflows returning.
BTC dominance rolling over from ~60% after a new high — in both 2017 and 2021 that was the alt-season trigger, and it has not happened yet.
Google Trends for a sector name rising from a low base — entry signal; at a multi-year high — exit signal.
signals.breakers: What could break the four-year pattern: ETF and treasury flows have already made this cycle's top lower and its bear shallower, so the next peak may be earlier and smaller than the halving clock implies; a Q4 2026 retest below $59,000 would push the whole timeline right by 6–12 months; and regulation (stablecoin, prediction-market and tokenized-stock rules) is now the main catalyst rather than the halving itself. This is research, not investment advice — position sizes and exits are yours to set.
